Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

*I'm 65, been working this same piece of ground for over forty years. Just 2 mu — about a third of a hectare. My wife passed, kids are gone to the city, so it's just me now. Can't do heavy work like I used to. But 2 mu is manageable if I pace myself and hire the combine for harvest like everyone does.*

*Wheat went in last October — already in the ground, came up fine before winter. Now it's spring, wheat is greening up, and I need to think about topdressing and irrigation. Then in June after wheat harvest, maize goes in right away. Tight turnaround, always has been.*

**Wheat (already planted last October):**
Put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before planting, like I always do. That gives the wheat its starter. Now in March-April I'll topdress with urea — about 15 kg per mu — right before jointing, and time it with an irrigation so the fertilizer goes down into the soil. The extension office tells us to split the N, and I've been doing that for years now, it works.

Irrigation — wheat needs water at jointing and again at grain filling for sure. If spring is dry, I'll do a third one at booting. Well is right there but the electricity costs add up. 2-3 irrigations usually.

Expecting around 450 kg/mu. Last year I got 470, year before was dry and I only got 400. Depends on the weather.

**Maize (planted mid-June, right after wheat comes off):**
No-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble — that's how everyone does it now, and I'm too old to plow. Hire the neighbor with the planter, costs me maybe 30 yuan per mu. Use a hybrid seed, the local agri-store sells the same ones everyone buys — Zhengdan or something similar, about 40-50 yuan per mu for seed.

Fertilizer for maize: I put the base compound down at planting, around 40 kg/mu of the 15-15-15. Then one topdress of urea at the big-flare stage, maybe 15 kg/mu. That's my usual. Middle school teacher's son (the extension guy) told us years back you can do it all at once with slow-release, but that costs more and I trust the split.

Irrigation for maize depends on rain. July-August usually has rain in Quzhou. If it's dry at tasseling I'll pump once. Maybe 1-2 irrigations total, sometimes zero.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once after planting to keep weeds down, I can't be out there hoeing at my age. Maybe an insecticide for corn borer if I see damage.

Expecting 500 kg/mu for maize. Good years I've hit 550.

**Cash-wise:** 2 mu is small, total input cost for the year maybe 600-700 yuan across both crops. I have enough saved and the wheat harvest will cover the maize inputs. I don't take credit.
